prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you pick the right type of lawyer and prepare to find one in Pleasanton, but I can’t make a specific, up‑to‑the‑minute referral. Below is a practical plan: what to do now, how to choose a lawyer, questions to ask at a consultation, red flags, and next steps I can help with.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care now (document injuries). Even mild symptoms can worsen later.  
- File or obtain the police report number.  
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries, and road conditions; names/contacts of witnesses; video if available.  
- Exchange insurance and contact info with the other driver.  
- Notify your auto insurer (tell them you were in an accident; don’t give a recorded statement until you’ve consulted counsel).  
- Keep a daily symptom/treatment diary and save receipts for medical bills, vehicle repairs, lost wages.

Statute of limitations (important)
- In California the normal deadline for filing a personal injury lawsuit is 2 years from the injury date (Code of Civil Procedure § 335.1). There are exceptions, but don’t delay contacting an attorney.

Which attorney to hire
- Practice focus: a personal injury attorney who handles car accident cases (not a generalist). Prefer attorneys whose practice is mainly auto-accident/PI work.  
- Experience and results: look for trial experience and a proven record of settlements/verdicts in similar cases. Cases that settle quickly or go to trial require different skill sets.  
- Local presence: a lawyer familiar with Alameda County courts, local medical providers, and the insurance companies that operate in the area. A Pleasanton or nearby (Livermore, Dublin, Oakland) firm is fine.  
- Communication style: you want someone responsive who explains things in plain language and tells you who will actually handle the work (partner vs junior associate).  
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no recovery = no attorney fee). Typical contingency rates run roughly 33%–40% depending on whether the case settles before/after a lawsuit is filed or goes to trial; ask about costs advanced and how they’re repaid.  
- Reputation and ethics: check the California State Bar for license status/discipline, and read client reviews and peer ratings (Martindale, Avvo, Google, Yelp).

Questions to ask at the first consultation
- Do you handle car-accident personal injury cases full time? What percentage of your practice is this work?  
- How many cases like mine have you handled? How many went to trial? Results (range of settlements/verdicts)?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? Will I deal with you or an associate/paralegal?  
- What is your fee structure and what costs might be advanced by the firm? How are fees and costs deducted from a settlement?  
- What is your assessment of the strength/value of my case and likely timeline?  
- How will you communicate with me (phone, email, text) and how often?  
- Can you provide references from former clients?  
- Do you have conflicts of interest (e.g., represent the other driver or the insurer)?

Documents to bring to consultations
- Police report (or report number)  
- Photos of the accident, vehicles, injuries, scene  
- Medical records and bills, or at least records of treatment and providers  
- Insurance information (yours and other driver’s) and claim numbers  
- Any correspondence from insurers or from the other driver  
- Pay stubs/documentation of lost wages, if applicable

Red flags to watch for
- Promises of a specific dollar amount up front or “guaranteed” outcomes.  
- Pushy sales tactics or excessive cold calls after the accident.  
- Unclear fee agreements or reluctance to put fees in writing.  
- Poor communication during the free consult (takes days to return calls).  
- No malpractice/disciplinary information available on the State Bar website.

How to find lawyers in Pleasanton / Alameda County
- California State Bar “Find a Lawyer” / attorney search (to verify license/discipline).  
- Alameda County Bar Association or local trial lawyers’ groups.  
- Online directories: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers (use reviews with caution).  
- Personal recommendations from friends/family who had similar cases.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short email or script you can use to contact several attorneys.  
- Prep a checklist of documents tailored to your case.  
- Help you evaluate 2–3 lawyers if you paste their names/firm links here (I can tell you what to look for in their profiles and how to compare them).

If you want more concrete next steps, tell me: when did the accident happen, what injuries did you sustain, have you seen a doctor, and have you already been contacted by an insurance company?
